issue.body:
# ATTENTION

> [!NOTE]  
> YouTube changes their detection scripts regularly. That means that sometime you can face the detection message.
> If all the following instructions do not work, please **email filters@adguard.com** or wait until any update is available. 

> [!CAUTION] 
> Please do not use another adblocker in the same time because using another adblocker can delay/lags the YouTube loading (e.g., AdBlock Plus and AdBlock)[^1] OR interfere AdGuard's filtering functionality.

> [!CAUTION] 
> Please do not use an userscript related to the bypassing YouTube detection message like [TheRealJoelmatic/RemoveAdblockThing](https://github.com/TheRealJoelmatic/RemoveAdblockThing).
> Recently, YouTube anti-adblock script added infinite dummy advertisements to try to neutralize the userscript. ( [TheRealJoelmatic/RemoveAdblockThing#264](https://github.com/TheRealJoelmatic/RemoveAdblockThing/issues/264) )

> [!WARNING]
> Please check that there no another web browser extension that has adblocking feature is enabled on your web browser. It can interfere AdGuard's filtering functionality.

> [!IMPORTANT]  
> Saving memory feature of your web browser or sleep feature of your operating system can interfere AdGuard's filtering functionality.
> In this case, please re-enable AdGuard's filtering by toggling the protection toggle.
> Following the instructions can be needed.

### The instructions
1. Force to update the filters by clicking the reload button in AdGuard Browser Extension/AdGuard mobile or update tray menu in your system tray. [^2]
2. Reload the YouTube webpage without cache by pressing <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> + <kbd>Shift</kbd> + <kbd>R</kbd> [^3].
3. Clear cache, cookies and site data of your web browser.
4. Re-open your web browser completely (checking your system monitor[^4] will be better).

[^1]: https://gitlab.com/adblockinc/ext/adblockplus/adblockplusui/-/issues/1576
[^2]: [AdGuard for Windows](https://adguard.com/kb/adguard-for-windows/overview/#tray-menu); [AdGuard for Mac](https://adguard.com/kb/adguard-for-mac/overview/#updates-check); 
[^3]: On macOS, <kbd>Command</kbd> + <kbd>Shift</kbd> + <kbd>R</kbd>
[^4]: Task Manager on Windows, System Monitor on GNOME Shell, KDE System Guard on KDE Plasma or Activity Monitor on macOS. 


Previous issue https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/issues/198973

issue.body:
### Prerequisites

- [x] This site DOES NOT contains sexually explicit material;
- [x] The problem occurs only when using AdGuard DNS or DNS filtering with AdGuard DNS filter, it is not caused by other ad blockers;
- [x] You're using an up-to-date version of AdGuard DNS filter;
- [x] Browser version is up-to-date;
- [ ] If a website or an app is broken, disabling AdGuard DNS filter resolves the issue.

### What DNS server do you use?

AdGuard public DNS

### Version

_No response_

### What DNS upstream(s) do you use in AdGuard apps or AdGuard Home?

Android Private DNS (dns.adguard-dns.com) — no AdGuard app, no AdGuard Home

### What DNS filters do you have enabled?

AdGuard DNS filter (default, via public DNS — no custom filters added)

### What browser or app do you use?

Other app

### Which device type do you use?

Mobile

### What type of problem have you encountered?

Missed ads

### Where did you encounter the problem?

https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.rovio.baba

### Add your comment and screenshots

An ad bypassed AdGuard public DNS filtering in the Android app Angry Birds 2 (com.rovio.baba).

The ad appeared as a full-screen black interstitial. Using Rethink DNS, I can see the connection was made directly to IP 34.160.81.0 (US, Google Cloud) over TCP/443 (HTTPS) — no domain name was used, which is why DNS filtering could not block it.

Device: Samsung Galaxy A36 (Android)
DNS: dns.adguard-dns.com via Android Private DNS (no AdGuard app or AdGuard Home)
Time of incident: approx. 07:00:42

Please consider adding 34.160.81.0 to the IP blocklist.

### Privacy

- [x] I agree to follow this condition

issue.body:
### Prerequisites

- [x] This site DOES NOT contains sexually explicit material;
- [x] The problem occurs only when using AdGuard DNS or DNS filtering with AdGuard DNS filter, it is not caused by other ad blockers;
- [x] You're using an up-to-date version of AdGuard DNS filter;
- [x] Browser version is up-to-date;
- [ ] If a website or an app is broken, disabling AdGuard DNS filter resolves the issue.

### What DNS server do you use?

AdGuard public DNS

### Version

_No response_

### What DNS upstream(s) do you use in AdGuard apps or AdGuard Home?

Android Private DNS (dns.adguard-dns.com) — no AdGuard app, no AdGuard Home

### What DNS filters do you have enabled?

AdGuard DNS filter (default, via public DNS — no custom filters added)

### What browser or app do you use?

Other app

### Which device type do you use?

Mobile

### What type of problem have you encountered?

Missed ads

### Where did you encounter the problem?

https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.rovio.baba

### Add your comment and screenshots

An ad bypassed AdGuard public DNS filtering in the Android app Angry Birds 2 (com.rovio.baba).

The ad appeared as a full-screen black interstitial. Using Rethink DNS, I can see the connection was made directly to IP 34.160.81.0 (US, Google Cloud) over TCP/443 (HTTPS) — no domain name was used, which is why DNS filtering could not block it.

Device: Samsung Galaxy A36 (Android)
DNS: dns.adguard-dns.com via Android Private DNS (no AdGuard app or AdGuard Home)
Time of incident: approx. 07:00:42

Please consider adding 34.160.81.0 to the IP blocklist.

### Privacy

- [x] I agree to follow this condition

# False Positive: First-Party Billing and Service Error Reporting Domains Blocked

This is a false-positive report, not an advertisement report.

## Summary

The AdGuard DNS filter incorrectly blocks several first-party service
reporting domains used by our browser-based service and applications on
Desktop and Mobile.

These endpoints are used for customer service usage metering required for
billing, service error reporting, diagnostics, operational status, and HTTPS
or WebSocket log transmission.

## Affected Domains

- `logreport-global-dual.cool*cloud.com`
- `logreport-global-dual.coolbcloud.com`
- `logreport-global-dual.coolhcloud.com`
- `detaillog-global-dual.coolbcloud.com`
- `detaillog-global-dual.coolhcloud.com`
- `detaillog-global-dual.coolccloud.com`
- `detaillog-global-dual.coolgcloud.com`
- `weblogger-wss.cool*cloud.com`
- `wslog-global-dual.cool*cloud.com`
- `wslog-global-dual.coolccloud.com`

## Affected Rules

```text
||logreport-global-dual.cool*cloud.com^
||logreport-global-dual.coolbcloud.com^
||logreport-global-dual.coolhcloud.com^
||detaillog-global-dual.coolbcloud.com^
||detaillog-global-dual.coolhcloud.com^
||detaillog-global-dual.coolccloud.com^
||detaillog-global-dual.coolgcloud.com^
||weblogger-wss.cool*cloud.com^
||wslog-global-dual.cool*cloud.com^
||wslog-global-dual.coolccloud.com^
```

## Purpose of These Domains

These are first-party endpoints belonging to our own service infrastructure.
They are used for:

- Customer service usage and metering information required for billing;
- Service errors, exceptions, and diagnostic information;
- Service health and operational status;
- HTTPS and WebSocket log transmission.

The data is limited to service-level usage, billing metering, error, and
system-health information. It is not used for advertising, ad attribution,
behavioral profiling, or cross-site tracking. It does not contain users'
communication contents or personal privacy data.

These domains do not serve advertisements or tracking scripts.

## Reproduction and DNS Comparison

The affected domain resolves normally through non-filtering DNS resolvers.

Google DNS returns a regional service endpoint:

```text
$ dig +short @8.8.8.8 logreport-global-dual.coolbcloud.com

logreport-global-dual.coolacloud.com.
logreport-sgp-dual-base.coolacloud.com.
8.219.127.160
```

Another public DNS resolver returns the following service endpoints:

```text
$ dig @114.114.114.114 logreport-global-dual.coolbcloud.com

logreport-global-dual.coolbcloud.com. CNAME logreport-global-dual.coolacloud.com.
logreport-global-dual.coolacloud.com. CNAME logreport-sh-dual-base.coolacloud.com.
logreport-sh-dual-base.coolacloud.com. A 106.14.181.205
logreport-sh-dual-base.coolacloud.com. A 106.14.52.63
```

The different real IP addresses returned by non-filtering DNS resolvers are
expected because the service uses regional DNS routing.

However, AdGuard DNS returns a reserved sinkhole address instead of the real
service endpoint:

```text
$ dig @94.140.14.14 logreport-global-dual.coolbcloud.com

logreport-global-dual.coolbcloud.com. A 198.18.0.25
```

When the domain is resolved through a non-filtering DNS resolver, the service
endpoint is reachable and log uploading works normally. When it is resolved
through AdGuard DNS, the endpoint is redirected to the sinkhole address and
log parsing and log uploading fail.

This confirms that the observed failure is caused by DNS-level filtering.

## Impact

Blocking these domains can cause:

- Log parsing and log uploading failures;
- Incomplete or delayed customer usage metering for billing;
- Service errors and exceptions not being reported in time;
- Delayed monitoring, troubleshooting, and incident response.

The issue is resolved when the affected domains are resolved through a
non-filtering DNS resolver or added to the allowlist.

## Request

Please review these rules as false positives and remove them from the AdGuard
DNS filter, or add suitable exceptions for these first-party service
reporting endpoints.

The rules can be found in the compiled AdGuard DNS filter:

<https://adguardteam.github.io/AdGuardSDNSFilter/Filters/filter.txt>

We can provide additional sanitized DNS information or connection metadata if
needed. We will not provide access tokens, private logs, customer identifiers,
or confidential customer data.


### Privacy

- [x] I agree to follow this condition

comment.body:
## Additional clarification

The DNS comparison confirms that this is a false positive in the compiled
AdGuard DNS filter.

The affected domain returns real regional service endpoints through public DNS
resolvers:

- `114.114.114.114` returns `106.14.181.205` and `106.14.52.63`;
- `8.8.8.8` returns `8.219.127.160`.

In contrast, AdGuard DNS `94.140.14.14` returns `198.18.0.25`, a reserved
non-routable address, instead of the actual service endpoint.

The different IP addresses returned by `114.114.114.114` and `8.8.8.8` are
expected because the service uses regional DNS routing. The important
difference is that the non-filtering resolvers return valid CNAME chains and
routable service IP addresses, while AdGuard DNS returns the non-routable
address.

When the affected domains are resolved through a non-filtering DNS resolver,
the service endpoint is reachable and log uploading works normally. When they
are resolved through AdGuard DNS, log parsing and log uploading fail.

The affected domains are first-party service endpoints used for customer usage
metering required for billing, service error reporting, diagnostics, and
operational status. They are not used for advertising or cross-site tracking.

# False Positive: First-Party Billing and Service Error Reporting Domains Blocked

This is a false-positive report, not an advertisement report.

## Summary

The AdGuard DNS filter incorrectly blocks several first-party service
reporting domains used by our browser-based service and applications on
Desktop and Mobile.

These endpoints are used for customer service usage metering required for
billing, service error reporting, diagnostics, operational status, and HTTPS
or WebSocket log transmission.

## Affected Domains

- `logreport-global-dual.cool*cloud.com`
- `logreport-global-dual.coolbcloud.com`
- `logreport-global-dual.coolhcloud.com`
- `detaillog-global-dual.coolbcloud.com`
- `detaillog-global-dual.coolhcloud.com`
- `detaillog-global-dual.coolccloud.com`
- `detaillog-global-dual.coolgcloud.com`
- `weblogger-wss.cool*cloud.com`
- `wslog-global-dual.cool*cloud.com`
- `wslog-global-dual.coolccloud.com`

## Affected Rules

```text
||logreport-global-dual.cool*cloud.com^
||logreport-global-dual.coolbcloud.com^
||logreport-global-dual.coolhcloud.com^
||detaillog-global-dual.coolbcloud.com^
||detaillog-global-dual.coolhcloud.com^
||detaillog-global-dual.coolccloud.com^
||detaillog-global-dual.coolgcloud.com^
||weblogger-wss.cool*cloud.com^
||wslog-global-dual.cool*cloud.com^
||wslog-global-dual.coolccloud.com^
```

## Purpose of These Domains

These are first-party endpoints belonging to our own service infrastructure.
They are used for:

- Customer service usage and metering information required for billing;
- Service errors, exceptions, and diagnostic information;
- Service health and operational status;
- HTTPS and WebSocket log transmission.

The data is limited to service-level usage, billing metering, error, and
system-health information. It is not used for advertising, ad attribution,
behavioral profiling, or cross-site tracking. It does not contain users'
communication contents or personal privacy data.

These domains do not serve advertisements or tracking scripts.

## Reproduction and DNS Comparison

The affected domain resolves normally through non-filtering DNS resolvers.

Google DNS returns a regional service endpoint:

```text
$ dig +short @8.8.8.8 logreport-global-dual.coolbcloud.com

logreport-global-dual.coolacloud.com.
logreport-sgp-dual-base.coolacloud.com.
8.219.127.160
```

Another public DNS resolver returns the following service endpoints:

```text
$ dig @114.114.114.114 logreport-global-dual.coolbcloud.com

logreport-global-dual.coolbcloud.com. CNAME logreport-global-dual.coolacloud.com.
logreport-global-dual.coolacloud.com. CNAME logreport-sh-dual-base.coolacloud.com.
logreport-sh-dual-base.coolacloud.com. A 106.14.181.205
logreport-sh-dual-base.coolacloud.com. A 106.14.52.63
```

The different real IP addresses returned by non-filtering DNS resolvers are
expected because the service uses regional DNS routing.

However, AdGuard DNS returns a reserved sinkhole address instead of the real
service endpoint:

```text
$ dig @94.140.14.14 logreport-global-dual.coolbcloud.com

logreport-global-dual.coolbcloud.com. A 198.18.0.25
```

When the domain is resolved through a non-filtering DNS resolver, the service
endpoint is reachable and log uploading works normally. When it is resolved
through AdGuard DNS, the endpoint is redirected to the sinkhole address and
log parsing and log uploading fail.

This confirms that the observed failure is caused by DNS-level filtering.

## Impact

Blocking these domains can cause:

- Log parsing and log uploading failures;
- Incomplete or delayed customer usage metering for billing;
- Service errors and exceptions not being reported in time;
- Delayed monitoring, troubleshooting, and incident response.

The issue is resolved when the affected domains are resolved through a
non-filtering DNS resolver or added to the allowlist.

## Request

Please review these rules as false positives and remove them from the AdGuard
DNS filter, or add suitable exceptions for these first-party service
reporting endpoints.

The rules can be found in the compiled AdGuard DNS filter:

<https://adguardteam.github.io/AdGuardSDNSFilter/Filters/filter.txt>

We can provide additional sanitized DNS information or connection metadata if
needed. We will not provide access tokens, private logs, customer identifiers,
or confidential customer data.

# False Positive: First-Party Billing and Service Error Reporting Domains Blocked

This is a false-positive report, not an advertisement report.

## Summary

The AdGuard DNS filter incorrectly blocks several first-party service
reporting domains used by our browser-based service and applications on
Desktop and Mobile.

These endpoints are used for customer service usage metering required for
billing, service error reporting, diagnostics, operational status, and HTTPS
or WebSocket log transmission.

## Affected Domains

- `logreport-global-dual.cool*cloud.com`
- `logreport-global-dual.coolbcloud.com`
- `logreport-global-dual.coolhcloud.com`
- `detaillog-global-dual.coolbcloud.com`
- `detaillog-global-dual.coolhcloud.com`
- `detaillog-global-dual.coolccloud.com`
- `detaillog-global-dual.coolgcloud.com`
- `weblogger-wss.cool*cloud.com`
- `wslog-global-dual.cool*cloud.com`
- `wslog-global-dual.coolccloud.com`

## Affected Rules

```text
||logreport-global-dual.cool*cloud.com^
||logreport-global-dual.coolbcloud.com^
||logreport-global-dual.coolhcloud.com^
||detaillog-global-dual.coolbcloud.com^
||detaillog-global-dual.coolhcloud.com^
||detaillog-global-dual.coolccloud.com^
||detaillog-global-dual.coolgcloud.com^
||weblogger-wss.cool*cloud.com^
||wslog-global-dual.cool*cloud.com^
||wslog-global-dual.coolccloud.com^
```

## Purpose of These Domains

These are first-party endpoints belonging to our own service infrastructure.
They are used for:

- Customer service usage and metering information required for billing;
- Service errors, exceptions, and diagnostic information;
- Service health and operational status;
- HTTPS and WebSocket log transmission.

The data is limited to service-level usage, billing metering, error, and
system-health information. It is not used for advertising, ad attribution,
behavioral profiling, or cross-site tracking. It does not contain users'
communication contents or personal privacy data.

These domains do not serve advertisements or tracking scripts.

## Reproduction and DNS Comparison

The affected domain resolves normally through non-filtering DNS resolvers.

Google DNS returns a regional service endpoint:

```text
$ dig +short @8.8.8.8 logreport-global-dual.coolbcloud.com

logreport-global-dual.coolacloud.com.
logreport-sgp-dual-base.coolacloud.com.
8.219.127.160
```

Another public DNS resolver returns the following service endpoints:

```text
$ dig @114.114.114.114 logreport-global-dual.coolbcloud.com

logreport-global-dual.coolbcloud.com. CNAME logreport-global-dual.coolacloud.com.
logreport-global-dual.coolacloud.com. CNAME logreport-sh-dual-base.coolacloud.com.
logreport-sh-dual-base.coolacloud.com. A 106.14.181.205
logreport-sh-dual-base.coolacloud.com. A 106.14.52.63
```

The different real IP addresses returned by non-filtering DNS resolvers are
expected because the service uses regional DNS routing.

However, AdGuard DNS returns a reserved, non-routable address instead of the real service endpoint:

```text
$ dig @94.140.14.14 logreport-global-dual.coolbcloud.com

logreport-global-dual.coolbcloud.com. A 198.18.0.25
```

When the domain is resolved through public DNS resolvers such as 114.114.114.114 and 8.8.8.8, the service endpoint is reachable and log uploading works normally. When it is resolved through AdGuard DNS, the endpoint resolves to the reserved, non-routable address 198.18.0.25 instead of the actual service endpoint, and log parsing and log uploading fail.

This provides evidence that the observed failure is caused by DNS-level filtering in AdGuard DNS.

## Impact

Blocking these domains can cause:

- Log parsing and log uploading failures;
- Incomplete or delayed customer usage metering for billing;
- Service errors and exceptions not being reported in time;
- Delayed monitoring, troubleshooting, and incident response.

The issue is resolved when the affected domains are resolved through a
non-filtering DNS resolver or added to the allowlist.

## Request

Please review these rules as false positives and remove them from the AdGuard
DNS filter, or add suitable exceptions for these first-party service
reporting endpoints.

The rules can be found in the compiled AdGuard DNS filter:

<https://adguardteam.github.io/AdGuardSDNSFilter/Filters/filter.txt>

We can provide additional sanitized DNS information or connection metadata if
needed. We will not provide access tokens, private logs, customer identifiers,
or confidential customer data.


### Privacy

# False Positive: First-Party Billing and Service Error Reporting Domains Blocked

This is a false-positive report, not an advertisement report.

## Summary

The AdGuard DNS filter incorrectly blocks several first-party service
reporting domains used by our browser-based service and applications on
Desktop and Mobile.

These endpoints are used for customer service usage metering required for
billing, service error reporting, diagnostics, operational status, and HTTPS
or WebSocket log transmission.

## Affected Domains

- `logreport-global-dual.cool*cloud.com`
- `logreport-global-dual.coolbcloud.com`
- `logreport-global-dual.coolhcloud.com`
- `detaillog-global-dual.coolbcloud.com`
- `detaillog-global-dual.coolhcloud.com`
- `detaillog-global-dual.coolccloud.com`
- `detaillog-global-dual.coolgcloud.com`
- `weblogger-wss.cool*cloud.com`
- `wslog-global-dual.cool*cloud.com`
- `wslog-global-dual.coolccloud.com`

## Affected Rules

```text
||logreport-global-dual.cool*cloud.com^
||logreport-global-dual.coolbcloud.com^
||logreport-global-dual.coolhcloud.com^
||detaillog-global-dual.coolbcloud.com^
||detaillog-global-dual.coolhcloud.com^
||detaillog-global-dual.coolccloud.com^
||detaillog-global-dual.coolgcloud.com^
||weblogger-wss.cool*cloud.com^
||wslog-global-dual.cool*cloud.com^
||wslog-global-dual.coolccloud.com^
```

## Purpose of These Domains

These are first-party endpoints belonging to our own service infrastructure.
They are used for:

- Customer service usage and metering information required for billing;
- Service errors, exceptions, and diagnostic information;
- Service health and operational status;
- HTTPS and WebSocket log transmission.

The data is limited to service-level usage, billing metering, error, and
system-health information. It is not used for advertising, ad attribution,
behavioral profiling, or cross-site tracking. It does not contain users'
communication contents or personal privacy data.

These domains do not serve advertisements or tracking scripts.

## Reproduction and DNS Comparison

The affected domain resolves normally through non-filtering DNS resolvers.

Google DNS returns a regional service endpoint:

```text
$ dig +short @8.8.8.8 logreport-global-dual.coolbcloud.com

logreport-global-dual.coolacloud.com.
logreport-sgp-dual-base.coolacloud.com.
8.219.127.160
```

Another public DNS resolver returns the following service endpoints:

```text
$ dig @114.114.114.114 logreport-global-dual.coolbcloud.com

logreport-global-dual.coolbcloud.com. CNAME logreport-global-dual.coolacloud.com.
logreport-global-dual.coolacloud.com. CNAME logreport-sh-dual-base.coolacloud.com.
logreport-sh-dual-base.coolacloud.com. A 106.14.181.205
logreport-sh-dual-base.coolacloud.com. A 106.14.52.63
```

The different real IP addresses returned by non-filtering DNS resolvers are
expected because the service uses regional DNS routing.

However, AdGuard DNS returns a reserved, non-routable address instead of the real service endpoint:

```text
$ dig @94.140.14.14 logreport-global-dual.coolbcloud.com

logreport-global-dual.coolbcloud.com. A 198.18.0.25
```

When the domain is resolved through public DNS resolvers such as 114.114.114.114 and 8.8.8.8, the service endpoint is reachable and log uploading works normally. When it is resolved through AdGuard DNS, the endpoint resolves to the reserved, non-routable address 198.18.0.25 instead of the actual service endpoint, and log parsing and log uploading fail.

This provides evidence that the observed failure is caused by DNS-level filtering in AdGuard DNS.

## Impact

Blocking these domains can cause:

- Log parsing and log uploading failures;
- Incomplete or delayed customer usage metering for billing;
- Service errors and exceptions not being reported in time;
- Delayed monitoring, troubleshooting, and incident response.

The issue is resolved when the affected domains are resolved through a
non-filtering DNS resolver or added to the allowlist.

## Request

Please review these rules as false positives and remove them from the AdGuard
DNS filter, or add suitable exceptions for these first-party service
reporting endpoints.

The rules can be found in the compiled AdGuard DNS filter:

<https://adguardteam.github.io/AdGuardSDNSFilter/Filters/filter.txt>

We can provide additional sanitized DNS information or connection metadata if
needed. We will not provide access tokens, private logs, customer identifiers,
or confidential customer data.

issue.title: Spam Gambling Sites
issue.body:
### Prerequisites

- [x] I checked the documentation and found no answer;
- [x] I checked to make sure that this issue has not already been filed;
- [x] This is not an ad/bug report.

### Problem description

How to reproduce:

Go to a spam site and enter your email address to be put on a spam list

Check your SPAM folder for Gambling emails
Copy (NEVER visit) the domains and paste them below to help out other members:

freeflowducts.com
trackallnotifrewa.com
trustus-eu.uk
adv.bestyofr.store

Wait to get how to reproduce message back from some ID10T.
Go to hospital for one day.
Receive another Github email from the same ID10T who has close it.

### Proposed solution

Someone to add these domains to the list to block or NEVER report any other filters to the Adguard people.

### Additional information

New spam domains added daily.

IN THE DNS FILTER, THERE IS A SPELLING MISTAKE IN ONE OF THE COMMENTS.

I thought it was the referrer, but it isn't working. I tried your rule, and that also isn't working.

I narrowed it down with testing down to the following required to be added:

```
@@||api.authsignal.com^$stealth
@@||myaccount.more.com.au^$stealth
@@||common-api.more.com.au^$stealth
```

But I'm now trying to figure out which stealth in particular is allowing this to work, as I believe you would rather have a particular one.

comment.body:
Okay, after a bit of time I figured it out, but I am confused.

This rule worked, but it was too broad:
`@@||au.api.authsignal.com^$stealth`

So after some trial and error, by mistake I found this rule to work:
`@@||au.api.authsignal.com^$stealth=3p-auth`

But the following rule did **not** work:
`@@||au.api.authsignal.com^$3p-auth`

Do stealth rules require `$stealth=` to be applied?
You were correct, it was due to third party auth, not the referrers.
Regardless, we now found the solution. Thank you.

issue.body:
# ATTENTION

> [!NOTE]  
> YouTube changes their detection scripts regularly. That means that sometime you can face the detection message.
> If all the following instructions do not work, please **email filters@adguard.com** or wait until any update is available. 

> [!CAUTION] 
> Please do not use another adblocker in the same time because using another adblocker can delay/lags the YouTube loading (e.g., AdBlock Plus and AdBlock)[^1] OR interfere AdGuard's filtering functionality.

> [!CAUTION] 
> Please do not use an userscript related to the bypassing YouTube detection message like [TheRealJoelmatic/RemoveAdblockThing](https://github.com/TheRealJoelmatic/RemoveAdblockThing).
> Recently, YouTube anti-adblock script added infinite dummy advertisements to try to neutralize the userscript. ( [TheRealJoelmatic/RemoveAdblockThing#264](https://github.com/TheRealJoelmatic/RemoveAdblockThing/issues/264) )

> [!WARNING]
> Please check that there no another web browser extension that has adblocking feature is enabled on your web browser. It can interfere AdGuard's filtering functionality.

> [!IMPORTANT]  
> Saving memory feature of your web browser or sleep feature of your operating system can interfere AdGuard's filtering functionality.
> In this case, please re-enable AdGuard's filtering by toggling the protection toggle.
> Following the instructions can be needed.

### The instructions
1. Force to update the filters by clicking the reload button in AdGuard Browser Extension/AdGuard mobile or update tray menu in your system tray. [^2]
2. Reload the YouTube webpage without cache by pressing <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> + <kbd>Shift</kbd> + <kbd>R</kbd> [^3].
3. Clear cache, cookies and site data of your web browser.
4. Re-open your web browser completely (checking your system monitor[^4] will be better).

[^1]: https://gitlab.com/adblockinc/ext/adblockplus/adblockplusui/-/issues/1576
[^2]: [AdGuard for Windows](https://adguard.com/kb/adguard-for-windows/overview/#tray-menu); [AdGuard for Mac](https://adguard.com/kb/adguard-for-mac/overview/#updates-check); 
[^3]: On macOS, <kbd>Command</kbd> + <kbd>Shift</kbd> + <kbd>R</kbd>
[^4]: Task Manager on Windows, System Monitor on GNOME Shell, KDE System Guard on KDE Plasma or Activity Monitor on macOS. 


Previous issue https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/issues/198973

